\ednentry{
  id = {EDN-98},
  title = {The prediction log stores only the fields a client sent, marked per row},
  date = {2026-11-04},
  milestone = {M6: Monitoring},
  topic = {Monitoring, API Design},
  participants = {Lukas Häußler (decided), AI agents (architecture proposal, implementation)},
  decision = {A record's \texttt{inputs} hold only the fields the client sent with a value, the set the model reads as known, and a new column \texttt{inputs\_\allowbreak{}sent\_\allowbreak{}only} is 1 on such rows.
Older rows stay as they are, with NULL, and the drift job reads only rows marked 1.
The schema version stays 1.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item The full request with its defaults plus a list of the sent fields: two sources every reader must combine, and bigger rows.
\item Only the sent fields, without a marker: old and new rows look alike, so the older rows, the VM load tests of 2026-10-31 among them, would read as real traffic.
\item Rewriting the older rows: lossy, because a \texttt{false} a client sent cannot be told from a default.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} The drift job compares input distributions, so a default nobody sent, such as an empty equipment list, would look like a real value.
The marker uses the existing path for added columns, which keeps a rollback working: the previous image names the columns it inserts and leaves the new one NULL, while a new schema version would make it refuse the file.
A record of the ten required fields shrinks by 166 bytes.},
  ai = {Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation, Solution generation},
  response = {Accepted},
  assessment = {AI found that the served \texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}basic} never reads the logged defaults, which are \texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}extended} inputs, so the old log broke FR-13's reconstruction promise for the extended model rather than any served prediction.
Lukas took the package unchanged.
AI built it; tests check a default sent explicitly, the in-place migration, and the previous image's insert on the migrated file.},
